gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a power station's low-load auto-off can switch off its AC outlets under small LED light loads: BLUETTI's AC180 manual says ECO mode turns AC output off when the load stays below a threshold the user can set from 10 to 30 W for 1, 2, 3 or 4 hours. ChatGPT's own table puts 10–30 W string lights inside that range.
standout_why: I tried to open the results ChatGPT got: the EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus manual (the aliyuncs PDF came back as image-only text, manuals.ecoflow.com showed only a logo, and the REI and device.report copies returned 403), gearranking.com's RIVER 3 Plus review (TLS certificate error) and BLUETTI's AC70 page (HTTP 429). None was readable, so I could not check line by line whether one mentions low-load auto-off. ChatGPT's answer itself sizes batteries for 10–30 W string lights and talks only about Wh and inverter losses. It says nothing about an outlet that turns itself off under a light load, which is why this is scored 2 and not 3.
decides: For outdoor lights, low-load auto-off matters more than Wh. A unit whose AC turns off below 10–30 W after 1–4 hours will leave a 10–30 W string dark partway through the night unless ECO mode is turned off. The page should tell buyers to check for (and disable) ECO or energy-saving auto-off, or to run low-voltage LED strings from the 12 V DC port. It should also rank models by whether their low-load cutoff can be turned off. That auto-off rule is sourced here for the AC180 only. For the RIVER 3 Plus, Explorer 600 Plus and DELTA 3 Classic it is still unsourced and must be checked in each manual before the pick is made.

findings.label: ECO mode low-load AC auto-off
findings.value: AC output turns off when the load stays below a user-set 10–30 W for 1, 2, 3 or 4 h (DC: 5–10 W); can be turned on or off on the screen
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 user manual, 5.1 FAQs Q4 (ManualsLib, printed p.16, English)
findings.note: Manual wording: 'When operating on ECO mode, the AC/DC output will automatically turn off if the AC180 is bearing low or no load for a while. You can set the power threshold of AC output and DC output to 10-30W /5-10W, respectively, for 1, 2, 3, or 4 hours.' This page does not give the default threshold or say whether ECO is on out of the box. ChatGPT's table row 'LED string lights, 10–30W' falls entirely inside the AC cutoff range.

findings.label: Capacity / AC output
findings.value: 1,152 Wh; 1,800 W continuous AC across 4 outlets; 2,700 W surge
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 User Manual (ManualsLib), pp.12 and 17
findings.note: Manual p.17: 'providing a total of up to 1800W AC power' and 'can handle a surge of 2700W'. The store listing calls 2,700 W 'Power Lifting Mode'. That mode is for resistive loads and is not the same thing as surge, so the two figures should not be compared directly.

findings.label: Discharge temperature range
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 User Manual (ManualsLib), spec table p.12
findings.note: Text as read: 'Discharging Temperature -4°F~104°F (86°F~104°F: @1500W Max.)'. Relevant for holiday lights running outdoors in winter. The Celsius column was garbled in the extracted text, so only °F is quoted.
